match_note: Nature Physics file (the paper had been reviewed at another journal before; that round is not included). Referees review the title 'Wigner polarons reveal Wigner crystal dynamics in a monolayer semiconductor', identical to v1; figure references (Fig. 1c, 2b, 2d, 3b, 3d, Fig. S5, Fig. 4) and claims (n_c ~ 7e11 cm^-2, Delta E_WP = a n^3/4, optical melting) match v1. The rebuttal's revised abstract adds 'in the frequency domain', absent from v1, so v1 is the pre-revision text.

concerns.quote: I encourage the authors to specify clearly the helicity of the pump photons used in the measurements presented in figure 3b.
concerns.summary: State the pump-photon helicity used in Fig. 3b.

concerns.quote: I suggest that the authors consider replacing the current panel (d) with Supplementary Fig. S5, which I find to be more informative
concerns.summary: Replace Fig. 3d with the more informative Supplementary Fig. S5.

concerns.quote: could the authors comment on the universality of the WPs? Do they exist in MoSe2 but previous studies missed them, or are they only present in WSe2?
concerns.summary: Explain why Wigner polarons are resolved here but not in MoSe2, and check whether they appear on the hole-doped side of WSe2.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Could the authors clarify how this mechanism compares to the interpretation put forward in the recent preprint "Spectroscopy of Wigner crystal polarons in an atomically thin semiconductor"
concerns.summary: Compare the phonon-dressed polaron picture with the competing particle-hole interpretation in arXiv:2512.16552.

concerns.quote: the Umklapp feature disappears under high pumping power, but the WP peaks remain... clarify how WP features can persist if the crystal itself is melted.
concerns.summary: If the umklapp loss means the crystal melted, the persistence of the phonon-dressed WP peaks is inconsistent with the interpretation.

concerns.quote: the same model will predict a lowering of the AP transition energy due to the smaller zero-point energy... But this effect does not seem to appear in the data.
concerns.summary: The WP model predicts an attractive-polaron redshift that the data do not show.

concerns.quote: the present work on WSe2 reports a substantially larger critical density of 7x10^11 cm^-2... which should reduce rather than increase the expected melting density.
concerns.summary: The melting density in WSe2 is higher than in MoSe2 despite the lighter electron mass, which needs explanation.

concerns.quote: Have the authors checked the consistency of the critical melting density in multiple devices or different beam spot locations?
concerns.summary: Characterize disorder and show the critical density is reproducible across devices and beam spots.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: The manuscript should explicitly state the hBN thicknesses in the active region, because gate screening can renormalize the electron-electron interaction
concerns.summary: Report hBN thicknesses and all device parameters since gate screening affects Wigner crystal stability.

concerns.quote: I am not convinced that the study on melting really contributes to a better understanding of Wigner polarons. The authors do not understand the underlying many-particle mechanisms.
concerns.summary: The optical-melting study is preliminary (heating or electron-lattice temperature mismatch may explain it) and should go to the SI or be backed by more experiments.

concerns.quote: I would also suggest that the author mention and briefly discuss the relevant recent study on the observation of excitonic Wigner crystals (arXiv:2601.19603).
concerns.summary: Cite and discuss recent work on Wigner phonons and crystal stability and on excitonic Wigner crystals.

concerns.quote: all measurements presented are based on continuous-wave spectroscopy without time-resolved or pump-probe measurements... clarify in what sense the present measurements probes the dynamics
concerns.summary: The claim to probe Wigner crystal dynamics is not supported by continuous-wave measurements alone.

concerns.quote: Could the authors extract the phonon dispersion as a function of moment k using the present data?... does this mode correspond to an acoustic phonon of the Wigner crystal?
concerns.summary: Clarify which Wigner crystal phonon mode the WP-AP splitting reflects.

concerns.quote: the n3/4 fitting of WPs does not show a resonance between the T- and S- branches from -0.5 to 0 V... uncertainty regarding extrapolating to zero splitting at zero density
concerns.summary: The n^3/4 fit is not supported at low doping; give error bars and explain the theory-experiment discrepancy.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the slope of the WPT and WPS branches decreases with increased excitation power... Does it reflect a modification of the quasiparticle mass or changes in screening?
concerns.summary: Explain physically why the WP slope versus density drops with pump power.

concerns.quote: Including a carrier-density axis on the same plot would help direct comparison between Figs. 2b and 2d.
concerns.summary: Add a carrier-density axis to Fig. 2d.

concerns.quote: could the authors comment on whether similar spectra are obtained when tuning the bottom gate?
concerns.summary: Check whether bottom-gate sweeps give the same spectra as top-gate sweeps.

later_concerns.quote: I am not sure whether this statement is necessarily true... I believe short-range-correlated Wigner-crystal domains can also give rise to similar Umklapp resonances
later_concerns.summary: The new claim that the umklapp feature primarily probes long-range order is too strong and should be softened.
